## Fixes

- **A deployment no longer strands itself when a worker starts.** Startup recovery and a deployment's queued message both work on one build. When recovery activated the build first, which a backlog of events ahead of the message made likely, the message found it already live, took that for a stale deployment, and marked the live build `superseded`. Events were then accepted and matched nothing, with no error, and a restart didn't help: only the next deploy did. Now one of them activates the build and the other leaves it alone. A live build leaves `ready` only through a new deployment. The manifest isn't loaded again over a live build, which also left a gap where events matched nothing and deactivated schedules armed since activation. A build already stranded this way comes back at the next worker start. Recovery now publishes `deploy:succeeded` too.
- **Events wait for a deployment in an environment of any size.** An event with no handler waits while a deployment is in progress, but the check read only eight builds, deployed ones first. In an environment with eight or more deployed builds it missed the deployment, and events were acknowledged as unhandled.
- **Two schedules of one function at one time both fire.** Hot kept one schedule per function and time, whatever its arguments, so a second `hot:schedule:new` due at the same moment failed with a duplicate key, and that call was lost. A schedule is now one call: a function, a time and its arguments. Sending the same call again returns the ID of the schedule it repeats instead of failing, a cancelled schedule can be armed again, and a one-time schedule that already fired stays spent. `hot test` arms a repeat the same way. Migration 030 replaces the index on both databases. Restart services with it: a build deployed through a worker of the previous version after the migration fails, and can be deployed again.
- **A name in `meta` reaches the build as its definition's full name.** The build manifest and the `meta` columns held a name as it was written, so `agent: Imported` stayed `Imported` and `::lib/Clause` kept its alias, and a nested name in a workflow's or agent's meta, such as `policy: {form: Complaint}`, became `{"$ast": "lang::Value"}`. Event handlers, schedules, webhooks, MCP tools, agents and workflows now all hold `::ns/Name`, the name the compiler already resolves. A run of a handler whose agent is imported from another namespace is now tagged with that agent, so it counts in the agent's health in the app. A path stays on the name, so `limits.port` no longer lands as plain `limits`. Builds made earlier keep the meta they stored.
- **Load order no longer decides whether a type alias is there.** A top-level value could call a function in another namespace before that namespace had run, and if the function named a type through an alias such as `Thing ::o::a/Thing`, the load stopped with `Function 'Thing' not found`, though `hot check` passed. Whether it happened depended on which namespace sorted first. Aliases of types, enums and variants, written in full or as a local alias, are now bound before any namespace runs, so this holds for namespaces that read each other's values too.
- **An agent's `mcp_servers` entry in the manifest names its server.** For an `mcp-servers` entry that's a name, `target` held a debug dump of the reference, which included the absolute path of the source file on the machine that made the build. It now holds the name, such as `::demo::flows/remote`.
- **`::hot::regex/capture` declares what it returns.** It was declared to return `Str`, but it returns `{match, groups}`, or null when nothing matches. Passing a bound result to a `Map` parameter stopped `hot check` with a type mismatch, and passing it to a `Str` parameter checked clean. It now declares `Map?`, and its docs describe the result.
- **A handler woken by a retry gets its own retries.** An event a retried run sent carried the sender's attempt, so its handlers started at that attempt and counted their retries from it. A handler woken by a last attempt got none. An event's handlers now start at attempt 0, whichever attempt sent it. A retry of the same handler still counts up, and `origin_run_id` is unchanged.
- **`POST /v1/events` outlasts a brief queue failure.** The API wrote the event, then tried its enqueue once. If that failed, for example through a Redis restart, the caller got a 500 and nothing ever processed the row. It now retries as a handler's `send()` does, for up to about 4 seconds, before it answers 500.
